core_equations: v1: a_t=softmax(W_router LN(m_t)); tau_t=0.25*tanh(a_t T); gamma_t=1+0.5*tanh(a_t G); h_t=gamma_t*relu(W_ff LN(x_t)-tau_t)^2. v2: tau_rank=0.20*tanh(m_t)*s_tau; gamma_rank=1+0.20*tanh(m_t)*s_gamma; tile rank values across FFN hidden groups; h_t=gamma_t*relu(W_ff LN(x_t)-tau_t)^2.
design_name: Memory-Selected Threshold Basis with Memory-Tiled Threshold v2
failure_notes: v1 passed smoke/grad and had a tiny validation edge, but training loss was worse and CPU throughput fell from 99.18 tok/s baseline to 57.11 tok/s. v2 passed smoke/grad and was cheap, but validation was effectively tied/slightly worse than baseline and median step time was slightly slower, so there is no clear loss or robust speed win.
next_ablation: Not recommended unless this family is revisited; then test v2 threshold strength 0.05/0.10/0.20 and a no-memory-residual variant where memory only shifts FFN thresholds.
novelty: The low-rank causal memory path changes FFN neuron activation thresholds and gain before the ReLU-square nonlinearity, instead of acting as an output gate, residual-only memory add, activation swap, or seq-by-seq attention.
why_help: The baseline low-rank memory block only adds causal memory features back into the residual stream before a static FFN. The candidate lets old-context memory alter which FFN neurons become active at each token by shifting thresholds, which could make the memory path influence feature selection more directly without attention.
